n: Antiguo Monasterio de la Cartuja de Santa Maria de las Cuevas
w: A Carthusian monastery on the Isla de la Cartuja that Christopher Columbus is said to have used as a base while planning his voyages west - a monk's cell doubling as a launchpad for the age of exploration. Its cloisters now hold the Andalusian Contemporary Art Center.
s: The monastery where Columbus planned his voyages
_facts: Religious building on Isla de la Cartuja, also known as Monastery of the Cartuja (Charterhouse)
Now hosts the Andalusian Contemporary Art Center (CAAC)
Nearby Isla de la Cartuja entry notes Columbus lived at the monastery while planning his voyage west

w: A working-class arrabal across the river from central Seville, historically separate enough that its people call themselves trianeros and still draw a hard cultural line between here and the rest of the city. Its potters and tile-makers built a craft tradition that shaped Sevillian style.
_facts: Neighbourhood and administrative district on the west bank of the Guadalquivir
Historically an arrabal, separated from the main city; residents called trianeros
Traditional pottery and tile industry, vibrant flamenco culture, own festivals

w: A late-15th-century palace mixing Gothic, Moorish and Renaissance style, still owned by the House of Alba and only opened to visitors in 2016. Poet Antonio Machado was born within its walls, and in 2011 the 18th Duchess of Alba married her third husband here.
s: A ducal palace that only opened its doors in 2016
_facts: Palace in Seville built late 15th century in Renaissance style with Gothic and Moorish influences
Belongs to the House of Alba, one of the city's major historic homes
Poet Antonio Machado was born here
Became a national monument in 1931; opened to tourists in 2016; Duchess of Alba married her third husband here in 2011

w: Andalusia's tallest building, a Cesar Pelli-designed skyscraper rising 180.5 metres over the old Expo '92 grounds on La Cartuja. Its curved podium buildings frame a plaza narrowing toward the centre, and the tower now holds a five-star hotel with sweeping views over Seville.
s: Andalusia's tallest building, on the old Expo site
_facts: Office skyscraper in Seville, also called Sevilla Tower, completed 2015
180.5 metres tall, 40 floors; tallest building in Andalusia and Seville, 8th tallest in Spain
Located in La Cartuja, former Expo '92 zone; designed by Cesar Pelli, with curved podium buildings
Hosts a five-star hotel, Eurostars Torre Sevilla; provides panoramic view over the city

w: Santiago Calatrava's cable-stayed bridge across the Canal de Alfonso XIII, built between 1989 and 1992 as part of the infrastructure push for Expo '92 to link the mainland to La Cartuja. Its single leaning pylon has made it one of the most photographed structures in the city.
s: Calatrava's leaning bridge, built for Expo '92
_facts: Cable-stayed bridge spanning the Canal de Alfonso XIII, providing access to La Cartuja
Built as part of infrastructure for Expo '92
Construction began 1989, completed 1992, designed by Santiago Calatrava

n: Museo de Bellas Artes de Sevilla
w: A former convent turned into one of Spain's finest art galleries, stacked with the Golden Age of Sevillian painting - Murillo, Zurbaran, Valdes Leal - across fourteen galleries and three cloisters. One is still built around the old convent cistern that gives it its name.
s: A convent turned gallery of Sevillian Old Masters
_facts: One of the main art galleries in Seville, collection from medieval period to early 20th century
Golden Age of Sevillian painting: Bartolome Esteban Murillo, Francisco de Zurbaran, Valdes Leal
14 galleries, three cloisters (claustro grande, claustro de los bojes, claustro del aljibe), and a patio

w: Seville's principal green area, a long stretch of parkland running beside the Guadalquivir - the city's default answer whenever anyone needs shade, quiet, or just a break from the stone and heat of the old town.
s: Seville's green backbone along the river
_facts: Public park stretching along the Guadalquivir River
Seville's principal green area

w: Built from 1682 outside the city walls on land seized by the Spanish Inquisition, it opened as the Universidad de Mareantes - a school training orphaned boys as sailors and navigators. Today it is the seat of the Andalusian regional government, a former naval academy turned government HQ.
s: An orphans' naval school, now regional government HQ
_facts: Historic edifice formerly the Universidad de Mareantes, now seat of the presidency of the Andalusian government
Construction began 1682 on land belonging to the Tribunal of the Holy Office (Spanish Inquisition)
Originally a school to educate orphaned children and train them as sailors

w: Commissioned by the city and built between 1916 and 1928 for the 1929 Ibero-American Exposition, it opened with a banquet attended by King Alfonso XIII himself and Queen Victoria Eugenie. Still city-owned, it now runs under Marriott's Luxury Collection.
s: A royal hotel built for a 1929 world's fair
_facts: Historic hotel on Calle San Fernando, designed by Jose Espiau y Munoz, built 1916-1928
Built for the Ibero-American Exposition of 1929
Opened 28 April 1929 with a banquet attended by King Alfonso XIII and Queen Victoria Eugenie of Battenberg
Owned by the City of Seville, managed by The Luxury Collection division of Marriott International

w: Seville's second-largest church after the cathedral itself - which, in a city built around one of the largest cathedrals on earth, is still an enormous claim. A Baroque heavyweight most visitors walk straight past on their way to its more famous rival.
_facts: Church in Seville, second-largest in the city after the cathedral

w: Built for Expo '92, this opera house sits close enough to the bullring, the old tobacco factory and the city walls to double as a stage set for Carmen itself - fitting, since Bizet's opera is set in Seville. In 1992 a rehearsal turned tragic when scenery collapsed, killing a chorus member.
s: An opera house built almost inside Carmen's setting
_facts: Opera house in Seville, main venue conceived for Expo '92, first performance 1991
Mainly devoted to opera, also zarzuela and other music; resident orchestra the Royal Seville Symphony Orchestra
On 16 July 1992, a suspended platform collapsed during a rehearsal, killing a chorus member and injuring 41 others
Situated close to the bullring, cigarette factory and city walls, near locations from the opera Carmen

w: A 42-to-45-metre Christopher Columbus, half-swallowed by a colossal cracked eggshell, sculpted by Zurab Tsereteli as a gift from the city of Moscow marking 500 years since Columbus reached the Caribbean. Locals just call it 'Columbus's egg' - the largest statue anywhere in Spain.
s: Columbus hatching from a giant egg - Moscow's gift
_facts: Monument in Seville by Zurab Tsereteli, popularly known as el huevo de Colon (Columbus's egg)
Colossal statue of Christopher Columbus partially enfolded by an egg-like shell
Gift from the city of Moscow marking the 500th anniversary of Columbus's 1492 Caribbean arrival
Reported height 42-45 metres; largest statue in Spain; inaugurated 1995 in Parque de San Jeronimo
